text:
aj: Heads up — after the kernel selection tweak yesterday we're seeing p99 regressions on the inference path. p95 unchanged. Suspect queue build-up for short requests.

katie: Which route? any recent config changes?

aj: /v1/generate route, kubernetes shard us-west-2, deploy-bot: kernel-picker v1.44 rolled at 02:15 UTC

sched-bot: Deployed kernel-picker v1.44 by @diego at 2026-03-10T02:15Z

diego: I changed kernel fallback ordering to prefer fused kernels for medium seq len. Also bumped max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 2048 to increase throughput.

yana: Logs show lots of queue wait spikes ~12-60ms for single-token requests. p99 jumped from 280ms -> 900ms.

aj: paste metrics

aj: ```
route: /v1/generate
p95: 210ms
p99: 920ms
mean queue delay: 34ms
kv cache hit ratio: 78% (drops to 54% during spikes)
kernel init time median: 18ms, 95th: 220ms
```

katie: KV drop looks suspicious — are we falling back to cold kernels often?

diego: Might be kernel cold starts when we route to fused kernels. They have bigger init overhead and worse tail.

yana: Also observed microburst of small token requests every min (cron-like). Continuous batching accumulates many tiny requests so max_batch_tokens increase could worsen tail.

aj: quick experiment idea: lower max_batch_tokens to 512 and reduce max_wait_ms to 4ms to favor latency at cost of throughput. Also tighten kernel selection to avoid heavy fused kernels for seq_len<64.

katie: +1. How long to run? 30m should be enough to see p99 shift.

diego: I'll roll a canary with following config on one shard:

diego: ```yaml
max_batch_tokens: 512
max_wait_ms: 4
kernel_policy:
  prefer: [lightweight, fallback]
  forbid_for_seq_lt: { fused: 64 }
```

sched-bot: Canary scheduled on shard us-west-2a for 30m by @diego

yana: Add KV hit tracing for that shard (per-request kv.key_count, kv.hit=true/false) so we can correlate.

aj: action: diego run canary; katie collect kv traces; yana correlate p99 and kernel init times. If p99 drops < 350ms revert more broadly.

diego: starting canary now

katie: collecting traces, I'll dump a heatmap at +10m and +30m

aj: if this works we'll consider an adaptive policy: auto-lower max_batch_tokens when queue delay median > Xms and kv_hit<Y%

yana: noted. let's keep an eye on cost impact too — throughput will drop but SLO wins.

diego: canary results in 35m: p99 => 360ms, p95 220ms, kv hit stable 80%, kernel init p95 90ms

katie: looks promising. rolling to remaining us-west shards with 1hr ramp.

aj: thanks — keep thread updated if anything weird pops.

diego: rolling now. will post post-roll metrics in ~1h
